description: K₂Na(SbO₃)₃ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pnn2 space group. There are two inequivalent K sites. In the first K site, K is bonded in a distorted hexagonal planar geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of K-O bond distances ranging from 2.68-2.89 Å. In the second K site, K is bonded in a distorted hexagonal planar geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of K-O bond distances ranging from 2.67-2.91 Å. Na is bonded in a hexagonal planar geometry to six O atoms. There are three shorter (2.52 Å) and three longer (2.59 Å) Na-O bond lengths. There are four inequivalent Sb sites. In the first Sb site, Sb is bonded to six O atoms to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing SbO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 52°. There are a spread of Sb-O bond distances ranging from 2.00-2.04 Å. In the second Sb site, Sb is bonded to six O atoms to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing SbO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 52-53°. There are a spread of Sb-O bond distances ranging from 2.00-2.04 Å. In the third Sb site, Sb is bonded to six O atoms to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing SbO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 52-53°. There are a spread of Sb-O bond distances ranging from 2.00-2.04 Å. In the fourth Sb site, Sb is bonded to six O atoms to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing SbO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 52-53°. There are a spread of Sb-O bond distances ranging from 1.99-2.04 Å. There are ten inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to one K, one Na, and two Sb atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OKNaSb₂ tetrahedra. In the second O site, O is bonded to one K, one Na, and two Sb atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OKNaSb₂ tetrahedra. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent K and two equivalent Sb atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent K and two equivalent Sb atoms. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two K and two equivalent Sb atoms. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two K and two Sb atoms. In the seventh O site, O is bonded to one K, one Na, and two Sb atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OKNaSb₂ trigonal pyramids. In the eighth O site, O is bonded to one K, one Na, and two Sb atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OKNaSb₂ tetrahedra. In the ninth O site, O is bonded to one K, one Na, and two Sb atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OKNaSb₂ trigonal pyramids. In the tenth O site, O is bonded to one K, one Na, and two Sb atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OKNaSb₂ tetrahedra.
